narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 63% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was denied.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class ranking in your third year of law school was the strongest influence, pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. Standing in the second decile is well below the average of accepted students (around the sixth decile), signaling that your performance placed you near the bottom of your class. Your first-year ranking in the second decile had a similar but smaller negative effect.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.10 worked in the opposite direction, modestly lowering the predicted risk of failure. However, this positive influence was not large enough to offset the impact of your class rankings.

Taken together, the model saw your relatively low standing in law school as the dominant signal that you would likely struggle to pass the bar on the first try.

What you should do next is focus on improving your academic performance and bar-exam readiness. Consider retaking key courses, seeking academic support, or gaining additional study time before reapplying. Strengthening your class rank and GPA in future semesters would directly address the factors that led to this decision.
